paragraphs: Here's the first thing, friend. Moses finishes a whole song and then says, "Take to heart all the words I have solemnly declared to you this day…" (Deuteronomy 32:46). He says they are "not idle words," because "they are your life" (Deuteronomy 32:47). God's Word is not decoration for a shelf. It's what you live on, like flour is what I live on, and I would not try a batch without it.

Notice who Moses wants the words to reach. He wants Israel to take them to heart so they can "command your children to carefully follow all the words of this law" (Deuteronomy 32:46). The Word isn't meant to stop with you. You hold it, you live it, and then you pass it on to the people coming behind you.

On that same day, the LORD gives Moses heavy news, and I think it's heavy for Moses too. He will see the land from a distance but "you shall not enter it," because both he and Aaron "broke faith" with the LORD at Meribah-kadesh (Deuteronomy 32:51-52). So the LORD takes holiness seriously, even with Moses, and we should too. Moses had already told Israel that God's words are their life, and the story isn't over yet, friend, so keep going.
